title: interactive-latency-simulator-and-load-profiling-notebook
content:
Goal / quick pitch:
- Small interactive tool + set of synthetic traces to help engineers reason about tail latency sources and the effect of batching/caching/kv-hit-rate on P50/P90/P99 for different model shapes.
- Not a full chaos rig — fast iterations, local runs with representative knobs, then scale to SRE perf cluster.

Why we need this (notes):
- Hard to reproduce customer-reported 95th pct spikes locally. Often appears only with multi-tenanted batching and cold GPUs.
- Existing load tests are heavy-weight and tuned for throughput; we lack a lightweight harness to explore: request-length distribution, kv-cache hit rates, intermittent client bursts, and placement-induced cross-tenant interference.

Design constraints / priorities:
- Interactive: change a few sliders and see P50/P90/P99 + simple waterfall breakdown.
- Config-driven traces: easy to encode burst patterns, ramp-ups, and mixed-model workloads.
- Cheap to run: can run on a dev workstation (one GPU) with mode: approximate behaviors (no full model compute, but latency components simulated) and on perf cluster with real model runs.
- Pluggable telemetry: emit JSON traces compatible with our Console traces so we can compare to production.

Core knobs to model / simulate:
- request_rate (rps) global and per-client
- client_burst_profile: (poisson bursts / periodic spikes / random outliers)
- prompt_length distribution: (short/medium/long percentiles)
- kv_cache_hit_rate: fraction of requests hitting prefix cache
- batching_window_ms and max_batch_size
- model_variant_mix: e.g., 70% redwood-7b-quant, 30% opt-13b-fp16
- placement_affinity: co-locate multi-tenant vs isolated pool
- gpu_warm_state: cold/warm vs warmed KV caches / warmed kernels
- network_rtt: avg ms between proxy and runtime

Latency component model (text diagram):
- client -> proxy (client-rtt) -> router (dispatch/queue) -> batch-window wait (batching) -> kernel/compute (model) -> kv/prefix-lookup -> serialization/streaming -> client

Simplified per-request latency = client_rtt + dispatch_overhead + batching_delay + compute_latency + kv_lookup_cost + serialization + network egress

Approx microbench numbers to calibrate from real runs (placeholders):
- dispatch_overhead: 0.4 - 1.2 ms
- batching_delay: depends on window and traffic; e.g., at 100 rps, window=8ms, expected wait ~4ms
- compute_latency: 4ms (redwood-7b q8) to 18ms (13b fp16) for short prompt
- kv_lookup_cost: 0.5ms cache hit, 8-12ms miss (if off-host retrieval)
- serialization+stream: 0.2 - 1.0ms

Simulator modes:
1) Fast-proxy-mode (approximate): simulate component latencies using sampled distributions + deterministic queuing model. Good for quick sensitivity sweeps.
2) Emulator-mode (real-model): send synthetic prompts through local runtime process + real model invocation (slower, accurate).
3) Hybrid-mode: compute small proportion of requests against real model to estimate compute quantiles; fill rest from sampled compute model.

Trace config language (sketch, YAML-like in the notebook):
- overall_rps: 120
- clients:
  - id: web-1
    rps: 60
    burst: {type: periodic, interval_s: 20, factor: 4}
  - id: mobile-1
    rps: 40
    burst: {type: poisson, lambda: 0.3}
  - id: batch-worker
    rps: 20
    prompt_len_dist: {short: 0.6, med: 0.3, long: 0.1}
- kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.72
- batch_window_ms: 12
- max_batch_size: 64
- model_mix: {redwood-7b-q8: 0.7, opt-13b-fp16: 0.3}

Things to watch / hypothesis to validate:
- Small increases in client rps with a fixed batching window cause P99 to jump nonlinearly because of stragglers and queueing.
- Raising kv_cache_hit_rate from 60% to 80% reduces P90 more than P50 (because misses have long tails).
- Mixed-model packing into same GPU (co-location) increases variance more than isolated pools even when average throughput unchanged.
- Kernel warm state matters mostly for p99 under bursty traffic.

Visualization ideas (cheap):
- Running plot: live P50/P90/P99 lines with markers where config changes applied.
- Waterfall breakdown: stacked bar per percentile showing contributions (batch_wait, compute, kv, network).
- Heatmap: batch_size distribution over time vs requests.

Experiment checklist (first pass):
- [ ] Implement basic event-driven simulator in Python (async loop, events for arrivals and departures). Use numpy for distributions.
- [ ] Config parser for YAML-style trace files
- [ ] Console exporter: JSON traces + minimal span fields to upload to Console for side-by-side with production traces
- [ ] Small CLI to run quick sweeps and emit CSV for plotting
- [ ] Hook to optionally send X% of traffic to local runtime (hybrid)
- [ ] Run small experiments comparing to perf-cluster load tests to calibrate constants (dispatch_overhead, kv_miss_penalty)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Should we model batching as a single global queue per-GPU or per-tenant queue? (tradeoff: complexity vs fidelity)
- How to represent multi-GPU placements (e.g., multi-tenant scheduling and preemption)? Start simple: 1 pool, add more later.
- How to get realistic kv miss penalty distribution from production? Need SRE sample export or use archival traces (request spans) — ask SRE.

Quick notes on implementation approach:
- Start with a minimal discrete-event simulator (Python, heapq for event queue). Simpler to reason about than full queuing theory formulas.
- Provide deterministic seeds to reproduce runs.
- Use a plugin interface for compute model: either a latency sampler or a local runtime RPC.
- Keep code in infra/perf/latency-sim with simple CLI: run-sim --config x.yaml --seed 42 --mode fast

Sample synthetic trace event (line-oriented JSON for quick ingest):
{"ts":"2025-11-10T15:24:01.123Z","req_id":"r-1750","client":"web-1","batch_wait_ms":5.2,"compute_ms":12.1,"kv_ms":0.6,"total_ms":21.2}

Notes to self:
- Talk to @Diego about pulling a small sample of p99 traces from prod for kernel-warm vs cold.
- Claire, will you help sketch a simple UI for the waterfall? Minimal first: stacked bars exported as CSV to plot.ly.

TODO short-term (this week):
- prototype event sim loop and a couple of config files (bursty, steady, mixed-model)
- add CSV exporter + quick matplotlib script for Pxx plots

Longer-term / wishlist:
- integrate with Console as an "Emulate" button: pick a saved route/config, run a sim to estimate latency impact before changing batch_window or rollout policies.
- ability to run therapeutic "what-if" tests: e.g., show expected P99 change if we increase batch_window by 4ms or if kv_cache_hit_rate drops 10%

References / inspiration:
- notes from perf-runner prototype (internal slack)
- academic papers on batching and tail latency (queueing with batch formation)

Rough dev time estimate: 5-8 engineering days for a usable fast-proxy-mode + basic plots. 2–3 more for hybrid-mode and Console export.

End of notebook.
